Policy Id: 106A fee incentive for narrowing the scope of registrations of trade marksStatus: On hold Priority: LowThe Productivity Commission's Inquiry into Australia's Intellectual Property Arrangements (“PC Review”) discussed the potential use of higher fees per trade mark class of goods and/or services to discourage overclaiming of goods and/or services.
- 
Policy Id: 123Accreditation and revocation of qualified persons/approved persons under the PBR ActStatus: Identified for action Priority: HighThe PBR legislation is silent on the requirements and processes for accrediting a PBR Qualified Person (QP), resulting in uncertainty.
- 
Policy Id: 45ACIP Designs Review Recommendations 18(a), 18(c) and 18(f) (technical issues)Status: Completed Priority: MediumIn its 2015 'Review of the Designs System' in Australia, the former Advisory Council on Intellectual Property (ACIP) recommended a number of legislative amendments to address technical issues identified by stakeholders.
- 
Policy Id: 116ACIP Designs Review Recommendations 18(b), 18(d), 18(e) and 18(g) (technical issues)Status: On hold Priority: LowIn its 2015 Review of the Designs System in Australia, the former Advisory Council on Intellectual Property (ACIP) recommended a number of legislative amendments to address technical issues identified by stakeholders.
- 
Policy Id: 101Act change to improve refund power for Trade marks and PBRStatus: Closed Priority: HighWhile the Patents Regulations 1991 and Designs Regulations 2004 permit the refund of the whole application fee or part of it on the basis of a wide range of circumstances, the Trade Marks Regulations 1995 and Plant Breeder Rights Regulations 1994 only allow a refund of fees in narrowly prescribed circumstances.
- 
Policy Id: 37Address confusion around 'registered' and 'certified' designs and the two-step examination processStatus: Closed Priority: HighCurrently, registration of a design occurs following a formalities check and substantive examination occurs only on request. If the design is found to have met the substantive requirements of the Act it will be certified and only then is it enforceable.
- 
Policy Id: 151Adjust Extensions of Time provisions of the Designs ActStatus: Policy development Priority: LowDesign rights holders and applicants can apply to extend a number of time periods in the designs legislation under various circumstances.
- 
Policy Id: 75Aligning the reckoning of periods of time in Part 13 of the Trade Marks Act with that in the Customs Act 1901Status: Closed Priority: LowThe Australian Border Force (ABF) enforces seizure provisions in Part 13 of the Trade Marks Act 1995 in line with its seizure practices under the Customs Act 1901.
- 
Policy Id: 40Allow amendment of the Statement of Newness and Distinctiveness (SoND) up to the point of certificationStatus: Policy development Priority: LowIn its 2015 Review of the Designs System in Australia, the former Advisory Council on Intellectual Property (ACIP) recommended that amendment of the Statement of Newness and Distinctiveness (SoND) should be permitted up to the point of certification.
- 
Policy Id: 7Allow Commissioner to seek external advice in applying a morality exclusion to patentability during exam or oppositionStatus: Closed Priority: LowShould an exclusion from patentability for matter offensive to the public be adopted, patent examiners would have to give consideration to ethical issues during examination.
